messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: elevated 5xx rate from ELB in eu-west-2a affecting inference ingress. Spike started ~15:12 UTC. Auto-alerting on-call.
Erin H: seeing this on the dashboard too — 503s and ConnectionReset by peer on a subset of targets. Investigating.
Jorge M: I can run a probe against the ELB health endpoints. Do we have the ELB name?
Erin H: `redwood-inf-ingress-euw2a-prod` — getting intermittent 503s when hitting /health and model endpoints, looks like some targets failing health checks.
network-eng-bot: Hitting ELB: average 5xx rate 8.6% in last 5m, target-group unhealthy count 6/48, skewed to az-a.
Kelsey L: paging PD now for EC2/ENI anomalies? This smells like instance network saturation or a broken NAT path.
oncall-asia: I'm up — taking triage. First things first: are these only in eu-west-2a or cross-AZ?
Matt P: traffic graphs show latency climb across eu-west-2a only; eu-west-2b/c steady. Connection resets correlate with a spike in TCP retransmits on instances in az-a.
Jorge M: running quick checks: ```
# sample
aws elb.describe-instance-health --load-balancer-name redwood-inf-ingress-euw2a-prod --region eu-west-2
# result: 6 Unhealthy, 42 InService
```
Erin H: grabbing instance IDs and SSHing into two unhappy hosts. Seeing kernel logs with repeated `ENETUNREACH` / `Connection reset by peer` entries for ephemeral egress.
Kelsey L: can we drain the unhealthy targets from the TG and shift their traffic to other AZs? We need to protect customer traffic ASAP.
Matt P: Starting graceful drain on the 6 instances in az-a now: ```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:... --targets Id=i-0aa...,Id=i-0bb...
```
incident-bot: Noted — automated runbook step: move 20% cross-AZ traffic to eu-west-2b until health stabilizes.
Erin H: Drain in progress. Observing 5xx rate dropping from 8.6% -> 3.1% in last 2m. Token latency still slightly elevated for some customers.
customer-sig: Customer Impact: intermittent 503s for a small subset of enterprise customers in EU region. No full outages but degraded inference success rate. We're notifying top-tier customers with a short bulletin.
Jorge M: AWS console shows spike in ENA errors for those instances; possible NIC firmware or hypervisor networking issue. Raising with AWS support — opened ticket 987654321.
Kelsey L: Escalation to AWS advised. For now we've shifted traffic and are scaling up spare capacity in eu-west-2b to handle sustained load.
Matt P: quick mitigation: increased autoscaling for dedicated pools in eu-west-2b and enabled fallback model variant on low-latency route to reduce token churn.
Erin H: On-call handoff planned at 16:20 UTC — I'll document actions taken so Kelsey can pick up. Current status: partial mitigation, 5xx rate ~1.1%, healthy target count restored to 48/48 after instance replacement/drain.
Kelsey L: Taking over at 16:20 UTC. Action items: (1) follow up with AWS ticket, (2) collect tcpdump + ENI logs from drained instances, (3) run postmortem checklist and start customer incident summary draft.
incident-bot: Handoff recorded: Erin H -> Kelsey L @ 16:20 UTC. Incident status: Mitigated (partial) — monitoring for recurrence.
Erin H: thumbs — saved traces and trace IDs in the incident folder: https://redwood-internal/archives/incidents/2374001122/logs. Will add the `dmesg` + `syslog` snippets.
Jorge M: attaching quick tcpdump snippet for the curious: ```
17:16:03.123456 IP i-0aa -> ELB  Reset, seq=0
17:16:04.234567 IP ELB -> i-0aa  Retransmit
```
oncall-asia: good job team. Keep monitoring; if AWS confirms AZ-level network degradation we will run full cross-AZ failover and consider longer maintenance window.
Kelsey L: noted. I'll update customers in 30m and kick off the postmortem draft. Closing active paging for now; will reopen if 5xx >2% for >10m. :white_check_mark:
